-   **IUCN:** Near Threatened
-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in marshes, agricultural fields, and urban areas.

## Natural history notes

A large blackbird characterized by its glossy dark plumage, long keel-shaped tail, pale yellow eyes, and iridescent purple, bronze, or greenish sheen, especially on the head and body. In Florida, it is found in marshes, wet fields, agricultural areas, pine flatwoods, parks, lawns, parking lots, and other open or semi-open habitats, often near water or human development. It feeds on insects, seeds, grains, fruit, small aquatic animals, and human-associated food, usually foraging on the ground or in shallow water and often gathering in noisy flocks.
